exposure: patient's initial preference for mode of delivery (VD/CS)
discussion of birth planning with an obstetrician
patient's decision for mode of delivery after discussion
outcome: actual mode of delivery (CS or VD)
cohort: The study included 125 pregnant women with a history of caesarean section who presented in their third trimester for a prenatal check-up.
finding: While 59.2% of patients initially preferred vaginal delivery (VD) and 57.6% decided on VD after obstetrician discussion, ultimately 62.4% gave birth through CS and 37.6% delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: The study found a shift in patient preferences for mode of delivery after obstetrician discussion, with a final outcome where a majority delivered by CS despite a higher initial preference for VD.
cross-section timing: From March 2021 to April 2022, during the third trimester for a prenatal check-up.
